title: Udayveer Singh v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
coram: Mahesh Chandra Tripathi, J. & Neeraj Tiwari, J.
disposition: Writ petition disposed of (without deciding merits) directing the petitioner to deposit Rs. 50,000 within three weeks, whereupon the Sub Divisional Officer is to fix easy instalments under Clause 6.14 of the Code
headnote: A consumer in financial distress who is willing to clear outstanding electricity dues may be extended the facility of easy instalments; Clause 6.15 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 obliges the licensee to extend such a facility to consumers in financial distress, and Clause 6.14 provides the mechanism for fixing the instalments. The petitioner, running a floor-mill (8.5 HP), challenged a recovery citation and sought instalments after adjusting amounts already deposited. Without adjudicating the merits, the Court disposed of the petition directing a deposit of Rs. 50,000 within three weeks, on which the Sub Divisional Officer would proceed strictly in accordance with law under Clause 6.14 and fix easy instalments.

holding_units.topic: Easy-instalment facility for a consumer in financial distress
holding_units.question: May a consumer in financial distress who is willing to clear the dues be relegated to the instalment mechanism of the Code rather than a merits adjudication of the recovery?
holding_units.holding: Yes. Clause 6.15 requires the licensee to extend the facility of easy instalments to consumers in financial distress, and Clause 6.14 supplies the mechanism. Without adverting to the merits, the Court directed the petitioner to deposit Rs. 50,000 within three weeks, on which the Sub Divisional Officer must proceed strictly in accordance with law under Clause 6.14 and fix easy instalments.
holding_units.limiting_facts: Floor-mill consumer (8.5 HP) willing to clear the outstanding amount; deposits already made but a receipt for part missing; recovery citation dated 7.5.2018 challenged; Court expressly did not adjudicate on merits.

principle_tags.application: A consumer in financial distress willing to clear the dues is entitled to easy instalments under Clause 6.15 r/w Clause 6.14, to be fixed by the competent authority.

not_decided.point: The validity of the recovery citation and the adjustment of amounts already deposited
not_decided.note: Court expressly did not adjudicate the matter on merits; left to the SDO to proceed in accordance with law under Clause 6.14.
